schema_facts: RequestId is string or signed int64, not a coerced textual identifier.
initialize accepts clientInfo and capabilities.experimentalApi; initialized follows the successful initialization response before other requests.
thread/loaded/list returns data thread IDs and nextCursor. thread/resume explicitly rejoins an already-running thread in memory, avoiding fresh rollout/bootstrap requirements.
Thread.id is the protocol thread target. Thread.sessionId separately identifies the session tree; inspection preserves it as provider_session_id.
Thread.canAcceptDirectInput is nullable; unknown/false does not imply structured prompt support.
TurnStartParams takes threadId plus input. Text input has type=text, text and optional/default text_elements. TurnSteerParams requires expectedTurnId and returns turnId.

ToolRequestUserInputParams includes threadId, turnId, itemId, isBlocking and questions. Question fields are id/header/question, default-false isOther/isSecret, and nullable options of label/description. There is no generated multi-select discriminator.

ToolRequestUserInputResponse is answers keyed by exact question IDs, each value containing an answers array of strings. Choice arrays and free text are preserved and checked, not synthesized as terminal keys.
CommandExecutionRequestApprovalParams includes exact thread/turn/item identity and startedAtMs; kind is command or writeStdin. availableDecisions, when present, constrains the offered decisions.

Command/file approval responses support accept and decline as request-only choices, separately from acceptForSession, amendments and cancel. The broker emits only accept/decline for explicit allow/deny.
File-change grantRoot has unproved session-root semantics; allow is rejected when non-null rather than silently broadening permission. Deny remains decline.
PermissionsRequestApprovalResponse grants only scope turn or session, default turn. No request-only allow exists in that shape, so item/permissions/requestApproval remains visibly unsupported.
serverRequest/resolved contains only threadId and requestId. It does not identify the winning responder or answer; it cannot prove an API response won a native/API race.
turn/interrupt requires threadId and turnId and has an empty acknowledgement. turn/completed and later serverRequest/resolved are independent lifecycle observations.

concrete_api.visibility: pub(crate) Broker and Prepared; parent registers the private codex module.
concrete_api.prepared_raii: Dropping an unbound Prepared removes and cleans only its own prepared instance. After bind, dropping Prepared leaves the live bound instance owned by Broker. Borrow the public fields; do not partially move a Drop value.
concrete_api.frontend_command: Shell-escaped codex executable and arguments only, without exec/env prefixes. Includes --remote unix://<owned-socket>, explicit --model, --ask-for-approval on-request, --sandbox workspace-write, --no-alt-screen, resolved --cd when supplied, and optional explicit resume thread.
concrete_api.frontend_env_secrets: No credential values. Values are frontend-only private paths, not shell-context environment overrides.
concrete_api.new_behavior: In-memory only; no Codex invocation, installation requirement, authentication read/copy or provider connection at ordinary daemon startup.
concrete_api.inspect_behavior: Retained in-memory observation only. No provider I/O or mutex held across provider I/O is used by inspection.
concrete_api.launch_failed_behavior: Records frontend exited/native-start-failed and cleans only that terminal's instance. Arbitrary supplied error text is not published; parent retains its separately redacted diagnostic.

closed_wire_contract.agent-open: controller, optional source/project/name/cwd, required explicit nonblank model, optional persisted resume_thread UUID. Unknown/incompatible fields are rejected.
closed_wire_contract.agent-inspect: terminal and expected instance_id; no control capability required.
closed_wire_contract.target: {terminal, instance_id, session_id}; session_id is the discovered provider Thread.id/threadId, never screen-derived.
closed_wire_contract.agent-prompt: target, control, text, intent=start|steer. expected_turn_id is required only for steer. Start requires idle/no pending/unresolved start; steer requires the exact active turn and never falls back to start.
closed_wire_contract.agent-answer: target, control, turn_id, item_id, request_id with exact string/int64 type, answers={question_id:{answers:[strings]}}.
closed_wire_contract.agent-permission: target, control, exact turn/item/request identity and decision=allow|deny for this request only.
closed_wire_contract.agent-interrupt: target, control, exact turn_id. Duplicate/ended/replaced exact-turn attempts are rejected without selecting a replacement.
closed_wire_contract.receipts: Mutations return a minted inspectable call receipt, not completion or task success. States queued/forwarded/applied/rejected/unknown and provider_ack are separate from turn lifecycle.
closed_wire_contract.inspection: target, provider_session_id, lifecycle, capabilities, exact pending rows with targets/provider_method/supported status, tombstones, recent calls, turn_outcomes keyed by exact completed turn ID, problem and resynchronization_required.
closed_wire_contract.completed_turns: lifecycle.turn_id is the ACTIVE turn and becomes null on completion. turn_outcomes[exact_turn_id] retains completed/interrupted/failed outcomes; a late old turn never replaces the active turn.
closed_wire_contract.events: Public/redacted kind+terminal+data tuples; take_events attaches instance_id. Parent assigns the existing global sequence cursor and snapshot/gap recovery. No second event service.

dispatch_and_identity: The worker owns each WebSocket and checks exact target/action semantics again when consuming the bounded dispatch queue.

Actual dispatch calls Authority::forward(call_id, agent-mutation) before provider I/O. Every retained Call owns the originating Arc<Authority>; late applied/rejected/unknown settlement uses that exact call and old authority without changing current ownership.
No topology/authority/state mutex is held across handshake/read/write/model I/O. Inspection stays responsive during provider backpressure.
Pending response identity includes terminal/instance/session/turn/item and exact typed provider request ID. Full-identity tombstones do not reopen on duplicate delivery.

The same typed provider ID may identify a new turn/item request, while old full-identity answers remain rejected. Because a reused-ID resolved notification omits turn/item, ambiguous resolution leaves the new pending request/call unknown rather than clearing or settling the wrong request.

Resolution of an ordinary request removes its pending row and retains a tombstone, but the API contender remains unknown when its winning response is not authoritatively identified. A uniquely attributable late provider rejection can settle the exact response call rejected.
Turn completion does not erase pending requests; pending cleanup can arrive later. Interrupt acknowledgement records request application/provider_ack, not interrupted completion.
Force/cancel/viewer detach are not broker mutations and issue no turn/interrupt, provider retry, reconnect, model turn or process stop.
Disconnect/degradation retains unknown work and blocks new unsafe mutations. Unknown request/native input settlement is never promoted to safe grant or task acceptance.

Explicit resume imports only its matching bounded persisted rollout into private history. This code path was NOT run during this task; no real auth was copied.
resource_behavior.cleanup: Unbound lease failure, native launch failure, terminal end and broker shutdown clean only owned resources. Uses the existing identity-checked runtime ProcessTree via the parent exposure specified below, bounded child reaping, socket shutdown and owned-root removal. Incomplete cleanup is reported as unknown/problem, never fabricated exited success.
resource_behavior.retention_policy: Only settled call receipts may be removed to maintain the recent-call bound. Unresolved calls and live identity tombstones are not silently evicted; exhausted accounting bounds fail/degrade visibly. Event overflow emits resynchronization-required.

helpers.capture_owned_session: pub(crate) fn capture_owned_session(pid: i32) -> Option<Self> { let info = process_info(pid)?; (info.session == pid).then(|| Self::new(info)) }
helpers.root_exited: pub(crate) fn root_exited(&self) -> bool { process_info(self.root.pid).filter(|info| info.identity == self.root).is_none_or(|info| info.exited) }
helpers.terminated: pub(crate) fn terminated(&self) -> bool { self.members.iter().all(|identity| process_info(identity.pid).filter(|info| info.identity == *identity).is_none_or(|info| info.exited)) }
